datasets.name: The involvement of the human prefrontal cortex in the emergence of visual awareness (Fang et al., 2024): sEEG, 6 patients
datasets.description: Stereo-electroencephalography (sEEG) recordings from six patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a visual awareness task with saccadic report. Near-threshold Gabor gratings were presented while awareness was reported via saccade direction, to examine the role of the prefrontal cortex in the emergence of visual awareness. The dataset includes per-trial behaviour, defaced T1 MRI, and source data with post-implantation CT and behaviour/eye-position files from patients and 10 healthy controls.
datasets.authors: Zepeng Fang, Yuanyuan Dang, Zhipei Ling, Yongzheng Han, Hulin Zhao, Xin Xu, Mingsha Zhang

datasets.name: Siena Scalp EEG Database: video-EEG monitoring of 14 adults with epilepsy (47 annotated seizures)
datasets.description: Scalp video-EEG recordings from 14 adults with epilepsy, acquired at the Unit of Neurology and Neurophysiology of the University of Siena, Italy. The dataset comprises about 128 hours of recording at 512 Hz using the 10-20 system, with ECG channels and 47 annotated seizures. It is a BIDS curation of the PhysioNet Siena Scalp EEG Database, collected for developing patient-specific seizure prediction and monitoring devices.
datasets.authors: Paolo Detti
datasets.eeg_reference: n/a (not stated in the release or the paper)
datasets.placement_scheme: International 10-20 system (with additional 10-10 positions Fc1/Fc2/Fc5/Fc6/Cp1/Cp2/Cp5/Cp6 and F9/F10 in most patients)

datasets.name: Leelakittisin2025: Sit-to-stand / stand-to-sit transition motor imagery dataset
datasets.description: A 60-channel EEG dataset with EOG and EMG recordings from 22 healthy participants performing sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit transitions under motor execution and motor imagery conditions. Each participant completed two sessions, with about 20 trials per transition class. It is described as the first public EEG dataset to explicitly target postural transitions, and supports research on neural activation patterns and brain-computer interfaces for lower-limb movement. This BIDS release was reformatted from the original Zenodo deposit using MOABB.
datasets.authors: Benjakarn Uengsawapak, Supavit Kongwudhikunakorn, Suktipol Kiatthaveephong, Wipamas Polpakdee, Rattanaphon Chaisaen, Poramate Manoonpong, Chanitsada Chuenchit, Gun Bhakdisongkhram, Theerawit Wilaiprasitporn

datasets.name: Leeuwis2021: Left- vs right-hand motor-imagery EEG dataset
datasets.description: A single-session EEG dataset of left- versus right-hand motor imagery recorded from 55 healthy, BCI-naive participants using a 16-channel g.Nautilus system at 250 Hz. Each participant completed one calibration run without feedback and three feedback runs, for 160 trials in total. The data were collected to examine psychological and cognitive predictors of motor-imagery brain-computer interface performance. This BIDS release was converted from the original DataverseNL deposit via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Nikki Leeuwis, Alissa Paas, Maryam Alimardani

datasets.name: Wang2025: Four-class motor imagery dataset (ZJU-MI-EEG / MI4)
datasets.description: A four-class motor imagery EEG dataset (left hand, right hand, tongue, both feet) from 15 healthy participants recorded with 62 channels at 256 Hz. Each participant completed two sessions on separate days, each with a calibration run and an online visual-feedback run. The dataset supports brain-computer interface research on deep learning-based EEG decoding and has been re-released in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Jiaheng Wang, Lin Yao, Yueming Wang

datasets.name: Thapa2025: Freewill reach-and-grasp motor-execution dataset from Thapa et al. 2025
datasets.description: A BIDS-formatted EEG dataset of self-paced (freewill) reach-and-grasp motor execution from 23 healthy right-handed participants across 49 sessions. On each trial, participants freely chose one of four cups (two water-filled, two empty) and the timing of the movement, yielding 6808 trials in four target classes. Recordings used a 31-channel scalp EEG montage plus EOG, accelerometer and audio-cue channels, and are intended for brain-machine interface research.
datasets.authors: Bhoj Raj Thapa, John Boggess, Jihye Bae

datasets.name: NeBULA2025: Standardized reaching motor-execution EEG dataset (NeBULA)
datasets.description: NeBULA2025 is a BIDS re-release of a high-density EEG (127 channels) and surface EMG dataset recorded from 39 healthy adults performing a standardized right-arm reaching task toward one of three illuminated targets. Each participant performed the task under three robotic assistance levels (free, low, high), supporting neuromechanical biomarker research for upper limb assessment. The data were reformatted into BIDS via MOABB from the originally published source dataset.
datasets.authors: Federica Garro, Elisa Fenoglio, Ilaria Ceroni, Iryna Forsiuk, Michela Canepa, Marta Mozzon, Alessandro Bruschi, Fabio Zippo, Matteo Laffranchi, Lorenzo De Michieli, Stefano Buccelli, Michela Chiappalone, Marianna Semprini

datasets.name: Ortiz2023: Motor imagery during walking with a lower-limb exoskeleton
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants performing kinesthetic motor imagery of gait, relaxation, and a regressive-count distractor task while walking with a fully assisted lower-limb exoskeleton on flat ground. Signals were acquired from 27 EEG and 4 EOG channels at 200 Hz. It was collected within the DECODED EUROBENCH sub-project and re-released in BIDS format via MOABB for brain-computer interface research.
datasets.authors: Mario Ortiz, Luis de la Ossa, Eduardo Ianez, Diego Torricelli, Jesus Tornero, Jose M. Azorin

datasets.name: Kueper2024: Unilateral vs bilateral movement-execution EEG dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 8 healthy participants performing self-initiated reaching movements with either the right arm alone (unilateral) or both arms synchronously (bilateral). Data were recorded with a 64-channel active-electrode system and are intended for movement intention recognition in exoskeleton-supported stroke rehabilitation. This BIDS release was reformatted from the original Zenodo deposit using MOABB.
datasets.authors: Niklas Kueper, Su Kyoung Kim, Elsa Andrea Kirchner

datasets.name: Batista2022: Motor-imagery EEG during NeuRow VR/haptics BCI training
datasets.description: Motor-imagery EEG recorded from 20 healthy volunteers during brain-computer interface training for a bimanual rowing task, delivered in virtual reality with optional haptic feedback. Participants performed cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery across Graz and NeuRow conditions, with and without head-mounted display and haptic feedback. Auxiliary physiological signals (ECG, respiration, PPG, accelerometry) were recorded alongside 32-channel EEG, supporting research on neurorehabilitation BCIs.
datasets.authors: Diogo Batista, Gustavo Caetano, Mathis Fleury, Patricia Figueiredo, Athanasios Vourvopoulos

datasets.name: IMUMIA2026: Multi-paradigm motor-imagery EEG dataset (IMU-MI_A)
datasets.description: A multi-paradigm motor-imagery EEG dataset recorded from healthy participants with a 64-channel Neuroscan system at 1000 Hz. Five body-part tasks (hand, foot, thumb, index finger, index-thumb pinch) were performed under a Classic Arrow paradigm and a Cue-Execution dual-stage paradigm. This BIDS release is a five-subject public sample of a 244-participant dataset, intended for brain-computer interface research on fine motor imagery.
datasets.authors: Jianxiu Li, Changming Wang, Chao Chen

datasets.name: Shin2022: Closed-loop 1D left/right motor imagery EEG dataset (live recordings)
datasets.description: A closed-loop EEG dataset of one-dimensional left/right motor imagery cursor control recorded from 10 healthy participants using a 16-channel dry-electrode system. Participants imagined left- or right-hand movement to drive a cursor toward a target under continuous visual feedback, completing 11 runs of 24 trials each while online control parameters were varied. The data support research on sensorimotor rhythm-based brain-computer interfaces and closed-loop decoding.
datasets.authors: Hyonyoung Shin, Daniel Suma, Bin He

datasets.name: MartinezPeon2024: Kinesthetic motor imagery at graded force levels
datasets.description: EEG recordings of kinesthetic motor imagery of a right-hand ball squeeze at three graded force levels (10%, 40% and 70% of maximal voluntary contraction) from 10 healthy participants. Data were acquired with a 14-channel Emotiv EPOC headset at 128 Hz, with five 5-second imagery cues per 40-second recording. The dataset supports characterization and classification of motor imagery force levels for brain-computer interface research. The associated paper (Journal of Neural Engineering, 2024) is by Martinez-Peon, Garcia-Hernandez, Benavides-Bravo and Parra-Vega.
datasets.authors: Dulce Martinez-Peon
datasets.eeg_reference: P3 and P4 (Emotiv EPOC reference locations)

datasets.name: Alawieh2025: Motor-imagery BCI dataset with transcutaneous spinal stimulation
datasets.description: A longitudinal EEG dataset of two-class (left vs. right hand) motor-imagery brain-computer interface training combined with transcutaneous electrical spinal cord stimulation. It includes 27 participants (25 able-bodied and 2 with spinal cord injury), recorded with 32 EEG channels and 3 EOG channels at 512 Hz. The dataset supports study of how spinal stimulation affects sensorimotor activation and BCI skill learning.
datasets.authors: Hussein Alawieh, Deland Liu, Jonathan Madera, Satyam Kumar, Frigyes Samuel Racz, Ann Majewicz Fey, José del R. Millán

datasets.name: PardoGarcia2026: Mu/beta motor-imagery EEG in chronic MCA stroke and healthy controls
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recorded during image-cued, two-class hand motor imagery and preparation (precision pinch versus closed fist) in chronic middle cerebral artery (MCA) stroke patients and healthy controls. Patients were recorded at baseline and after rehabilitation, and eight healthy controls were recorded once. It supports analysis of mu and beta oscillatory changes (event-related desynchronization) associated with motor imagery and rehabilitation. The data were recorded with 63 BrainVision channels at 1000 Hz and re-released in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Rebeca Pardo-Garcia, Maria Ruiz-Izquierdo, Mercedes Garcia de la Vega, Rocio Calvillo, George Kontaxakis, Eva M. Moreno, M. A. Pozo

datasets.name: NeuroTUMBCI2025: Motor imagery dataset from the neuroTUM 2024 Cybathlon BCI
datasets.description: A mobile EEG motor imagery dataset from two pilots, one tetraplegic and one able-bodied, recorded during development of the neuroTUM brain-computer interface for the 2024 Cybathlon BCI race. Data were acquired with a 24-channel wireless Smarting mobi system at 250 Hz using an arrow-cue paradigm with subject-specific sets of three mental tasks (rest, hand and/or foot motor imagery). The dataset is re-released in BIDS format with HED annotations via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Isabel W. Tscherniak, Niels C. Thiemann, Ana McWhinnie-Fernandez, Iustin Curcean, Leon L. J. Jokinen, Sadat Hodzic, Thomas E. Huber, Daniel Pavlov, Manuel Methasani, Pietro Marcolongo, Glenn V. Krafczyk, Oscar Osvaldo Soto Rivera, Thien Le, Flaminia Pallotti, Enrico A. Fazzi

datasets.name: Jia2019: Motor-imagery EEG dataset for stroke patients (Jia 2019)
datasets.description: This dataset contains 63-channel EEG recorded at 512 Hz from 15 stroke patients performing cue-based left-hand versus right-hand motor imagery, with 40 trials per class. For each patient one hand is paretic and the other unaffected, and both were imagined. It is a BIDS re-release of the original figshare deposit, prepared via MOABB with HED event annotations, and is intended for brain-computer interface and neurorehabilitation research.
datasets.authors: Tianyu Jia

datasets.name: NETBCI2026: NETBCI: longitudinal right-hand motor imagery vs rest BCI training
datasets.description: A longitudinal EEG dataset of right-hand motor imagery versus rest during brain-computer interface (BCI) training. Nineteen healthy participants completed four sessions on four separate days, with six online feedback runs per session using a one-dimensional two-target cursor task. EEG was recorded from 74 channels at 250 Hz alongside a MEG system, and the dataset contains about 14,400 trials. It supports studies of BCI learning and neurofeedback.
datasets.authors: Marie-Constance Corsi, Christophe Gitton, Juliana Gonzalez-Astudillo, Ari E. Kahn, Laurent Hugueville, Denis Schwartz, Nathalie George, Mario Chavez, Sophie Dupont, Danielle S. Bassett, Fabrizio De Vico Fallani

datasets.name: PoloHortiguela2025: Motor imagery of ankle dorsiflexion/plantarflexion dataset
datasets.description: Open-loop EEG dataset of kinesthetic motor imagery of ankle dorsiflexion/plantarflexion alternated with relaxation, recorded from six healthy participants. Each participant completed two sessions, one with a static and one with a moving lower-limb exoskeleton. The recordings contain 28 EEG channels and 4 EOG channels sampled at 250 Hz. This is a BIDS re-release of the Zenodo deposit, produced via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Cristina Polo-Hortiguela, Mario Ortiz, Eduardo Ianez, Jose M. Azorin

datasets.name: Pan2025: Cross-session motor imagery dataset from Pan et al. 2025
datasets.description: A cross-session motor imagery EEG dataset from 10 healthy participants who performed cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery across two sessions. Recordings used 28 EEG channels sampled at 250 Hz with a Neuroscan SynAmps2 amplifier, with roughly 180 trials per session. In session 2, test trials included online feedback. The data were re-released in BIDS format via MOABB for brain-computer interface research.
datasets.authors: Lincong Pan

datasets.name: WRCC2023_MI_C: Three-class motor imagery dataset from the World Robot Contest 2023 (MI-C)
datasets.description: Three-class motor imagery (left hand, right hand, feet) EEG dataset from the MI-C track of the 2023 World Robot Contest BCI competition. It contains recordings from 8 participants, including 2 stroke patients, with 90 cue-based trials each, acquired with a 59-channel EEG system at 1000 Hz. This BIDS release was produced via MOABB from the original Harvard Dataverse deposit.
datasets.authors: WRCC2023

datasets.name: WRCC2023_MI_B: Three-class motor imagery dataset (MI-B) of the BCI competition WRCC2023
datasets.description: Three-class motor imagery EEG dataset (MI-B) from the BCI competition at the 2023 World Robot Contest (WRCC2023). It contains recordings from nine subjects, two of them stroke patients and seven healthy, performing cued imagery of left hand, right hand and feet movements (30 trials per class). Signals were recorded with a 59-channel Neuracle EEG system at 1000 Hz and re-released in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: WRCC2023

datasets.name: WRCC2023_MI_A: WRCC2023 MI-A three-class motor imagery dataset
datasets.description: A three-class motor imagery EEG dataset (left hand, right hand, feet) from the MI-A track of the 2023 World Robot Contest BCI competition. It includes recordings from nine participants, two of whom are stroke patients, with 90 cued 4-second imagery trials each (30 per class). Data were acquired at 1000 Hz from 59 EEG channels using a Neuracle wireless system and re-released in BIDS format with HED annotations via MOABB.
datasets.authors: WRCC2023

datasets.name: MIMED2024: Motor Imagery MIMED dataset from Wirawan et al. 2024
datasets.description: EEG recordings of motor imagery and motor execution for six activities (raising and lowering each hand, standing and sitting) from 30 healthy participants over two sessions. Data were acquired with a 14-channel Emotiv EPOC X headset at 128 Hz. This BIDS re-release, produced via MOABB, exposes a 3-class imagery task (left hand, right hand, trunk) for brain-computer interface research. The distributed imagery files carry no per-repetition activity label, so only folder-level 3-class labels are available.
datasets.authors: I Made Agus Wirawan, Dechrit Maneetham, I Gede Mahendra Darmawiguna, Arnon Niyomphol, Pakornkiat Sawetmethikul, Padma Nyoman Crisnapati, Yamin Thwe, Ni Nyoman Mestri Agustini

datasets.name: Kodera2023: Left/right-hand motor-imagery EEG dataset
datasets.description: A left/right-hand motor-imagery EEG dataset from 29 healthy participants recorded at the University of West Bohemia for brain-computer interface research. Participants performed cue-based single-class imagery of left- or right-hand movement, with four runs per session. The data were recorded with BrainVision hardware and re-released in BIDS format through MOABB, with HED event annotations.
datasets.authors: Jakub Kodera, Roman Moucek, Pavel Moutner, Pavel Mochura, Josef Yassin Saleh, Petr Bruha, Jana Solcova, Lukas Vareka, Pavel Snejdar

datasets.name: Pan2023: Cross-session motor imagery dataset from Pan et al. 2023
datasets.description: A cross-session motor imagery EEG dataset from 14 healthy participants who performed cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery on two separate days. Data were recorded with 28 EEG channels at 250 Hz and comprise 60 trials per class per session. The dataset supports research on brain-computer interface decoding and cross-session variability, and it is distributed here in BIDS format with HED event annotations.
datasets.authors: Lincong Pan, Kun Wang, Lichao Xu, Xinwei Sun, Weibo Yi, Minpeng Xu, Dong Ming

datasets.name: Training datasets for epilepsy analysis: sliding-window features derived from the Freiburg intracranial EEG database (Riccio et al. 2024), processed-data release
datasets.description: This derivative dataset redistributes 20 per-patient feature tables computed from the Freiburg intracranial EEG database. Each row is a 2-second sliding window (1-second step) with 1080 univariate and bivariate features extracted from six electrodes across six frequency bands. Windows are labelled as pre-ictal, ictal, post-ictal or inter-ictal, so the tables can be used to train machine-learning models for epileptic seizure analysis. The CSV files are byte-identical to the source Zenodo record, and no raw recordings are included.
datasets.authors: Christian Riccio, Angelo Martone, Gaetano Zazzaro, Luigi Pavone

datasets.name: Categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone: ECoG auditory oddball in 6 epilepsy patients (Si, Zhou & Hong 2017)
datasets.description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from six patients with medically intractable epilepsy who passively listened to a two-deviant auditory oddball sequence of synthesized Mandarin syllables. The paradigm used a tone continuum with a frequent standard and two deviants, one cross-category and one within-category, at equal physical distance from the standard. The data support investigation of the cortical network underlying categorical perception of Chinese lexical tone. They are reorganized into iEEG-BIDS without signal processing.
datasets.authors: Xiaopeng Si, Wenjing Zhou, Bo Hong

datasets.name: Task-SEEG recordings from epilepsy patients performing a visual working memory task (Tian, Figshare 32189838)
datasets.description: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from seven patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a visual working memory task. Recordings were acquired at 2048 Hz from clinically placed depth electrodes, including contacts in the hippocampus and frontal eye field. This BIDS iEEG copy provides continuous EDF recordings with de-identified headers and corrected channel types.
datasets.authors: Ziwei Tian

datasets.name: MOVING2024: Motor imagery / motor execution dataset from the MOVING study
datasets.description: A multi-modal dataset of 32-channel dry-electrode EEG recorded together with Virtual Glove hand-kinematic tracking during motor imagery and motor execution of three right-hand movements (open/close, wrist rotation, finger tapping). Eleven healthy participants completed a rest, motor imagery, motor execution sequence with eight repetitions of the triplet. This BIDS re-release was produced via MOABB from the published MOVING dataset.
datasets.authors: Enrico Mattei, Daniele Lozzi, Alessandro Di Matteo, Alessia Cipriani, Costanzo Manes, Giuseppe Placidi

datasets.name: BrainQuake example SEEG data: ictal and interictal stereo-EEG from 8 epilepsy patients (Tsinghua Yuquan Hospital)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG (SEEG) recordings from 8 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, collected at the Epilepsy Center of Tsinghua Yuquan Hospital during pre-surgical monitoring. The dataset contains 71-second ictal clips and interictal segments of up to about 2 hours per patient, sampled at 2000 Hz. It was released as example data for the BrainQuake toolbox and reorganised into iEEG-BIDS without signal processing. The data support analyses such as the Epileptogenicity Index and high-frequency event (HFO) detection.
datasets.authors: Kang Wang

datasets.name: MILimbEEG: Motor and motor-imagery limb EEG dataset (MILimbEEG)
datasets.description: MILimbEEG is an EEG dataset from 60 volunteers performing and imagining upper- and lower-limb movements (hand closing and dorsal/plantar foot flexion, left and right), plus baseline eyes-open and rest conditions. It comprises over 8,680 four-second recordings acquired with a 16-channel dry-electrode OpenBCI Cyton+Daisy system at 125 Hz. The cohort includes healthy participants and some clinical cases, such as amputees and post-COVID-19 participants. The dataset supports brain-computer interface research on motor execution and motor imagery.
datasets.authors: Victor Asanza, Daniel Montoya, Leandro L. Lorente-Leyva, Diego H. Peluffo-Ordonez, Kleber Gonzalez

datasets.name: Vagaja2023: Motor-imagery EEG during embodiment-primed MI-BCI training in VR
datasets.description: This dataset contains motor-imagery EEG, bipolar EMG, skin temperature and accelerometry recorded from 26 healthy volunteers performing cued left- vs right-hand motor imagery during MI-BCI training in immersive virtual reality. Participants were randomized to an embodiment-primed (virtual hand illusion) group or a non-embodied control group, each completing one run of 40 trials. The data were re-released in BIDS format via MOABB from the original Zenodo deposit.
datasets.authors: Katarina Vagaja, Athanasios Vourvopoulos

datasets.name: PROTEUS BCI Bordeaux — EEG/EMG Foundation Challenge 2026, Track 02
datasets.description: EEG dataset from the PROTEUS brain-computer interface (BCI) project in Bordeaux, released for the EEG/EMG Foundation Challenge 2026 (Track 02). It contains recordings from 10 participants across 14 sessions (112 runs) performing three cued mental tasks: kinesthetic motor imagery, mental subtraction and word generation. Runs include resting baselines, calibration runs with sham feedback and online runs with real feedback, using Graz and BrainHero interfaces.
datasets.authors: Dreyer Pauline, Bourdil Manon, Bechon Loic, Kojima Simon, Velut Sebastien, Rimbert Sebastien, Roy Raphaëlle, Lotte Fabien

datasets.name: Muse Sleep-Onset EEG — EEG/EMG Foundation Challenge 2026, Track 03
datasets.description: This dataset contains 540 at-home, four-channel (TP9, AF7, AF8, TP10) EEG recordings from 203 participants, collected with Muse headbands at 128 Hz. It was prepared for Track 03 (Sleep onset) of the EEG/EMG Foundation Challenge 2026, where the task is to predict time remaining until the first N2 sleep epoch from EEG recorded up to the prediction time. Each recording carries a single N2-onset annotation, and the deposit includes a train/test split and signal-quality flags.
datasets.authors: Muse Team
datasets.placement_scheme: Four headband EEG channels: TP9, AF7, AF8, TP10 (extended 10/20 labels).

datasets.name: EEG and hedonic responses to sonic-seasoning soundscapes
datasets.description: This dataset contains consumer-grade 14-channel EEG (EMOTIV EPOC X) recorded from 30 sessions while participants completed eyes-open and eyes-closed baselines and listened to about 17 s of two sonic-seasoning soundscapes (jungle and deconstruct). Liking ratings and baseline-state survey items are provided in participants.tsv, with the stimulus audio and the manufacturer's contact and EEG quality signals. An EEGLAB-ready processed version of the two soundscape conditions is included as a derivative.
datasets.authors: Attila Pohlmann, Felipe Reinoso-Carvalho, Brayan Rodríguez

datasets.name: STRUM: Small Team Reconnaissance Urban Missions
datasets.description: STRUM is a dyadic neuroergonomics dataset in which pairs of participants perform a collaborative urban-reconnaissance task while a time-synchronized multimodal sensor suite records both members simultaneously via Lab Streaming Layer. It covers 33 sessions and 66 participants, with high-density EEG, EMG, ECG/EOG, motion capture, eye-tracking, force plate and controller behavior. Each participant has their own subject directory, and the pairing is encoded in participants.tsv so that analyses can split by pair.
datasets.authors: Anonymous (withheld until publication)
datasets.eeg_reference: BioSemi CMS/DRL active reference (recorded reference-free); EX1/EX2 are the mastoid electrodes available for offline re-referencing
datasets.placement_scheme: BioSemi 256-channel cap (banks A-H + EX1-8); standard external-channel assignment (2 ECG, 2 EOG)

datasets.name: ZuCo 2.0: EEG and Eye-Tracking during Natural Reading and Annotation
datasets.description: ZuCo 2.0 provides simultaneous 128-channel EEG and eye-tracking recordings from adult native English speakers reading natural Wikipedia sentences. Two paradigms are included: normal reading and task-specific reading with annotation of semantic relations. The data are organized in BIDS with gaze and pupil samples as physiological recordings and fixations, saccades and blinks as events.
datasets.authors: Nora Hollenstein, Marius Tröndle, Ce Zhang, Nicolas Langer

datasets.name: ZuCo 1.0: Simultaneous EEG and Eye-Tracking during Natural Reading
datasets.description: ZuCo 1.0 is a BIDS-formatted dataset of simultaneous 128-channel EEG and eye-tracking recorded while adult native English speakers read natural sentences. Three reading tasks are included: sentiment reading of movie-review sentences, normal reading of Wikipedia sentences, and task-specific reading with semantic relation annotation. The dataset supports research on the neural and oculomotor correlates of natural language comprehension.
datasets.authors: Nora Hollenstein, Jonathan Rotsztejn, Marius Tröndle, Andreas Pedroni, Ce Zhang, Nicolas Langer

datasets.name: EEG: 3-Stim Auditory Oddball and Rest in Parkinson's
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 25 patients with Parkinson's disease and 25 matched controls during resting state (eyes open and eyes closed) and a three-stimulus auditory oddball task. Patients were recorded twice, one week apart, once ON and once OFF dopaminergic medication, while controls were recorded once. Accelerometer data from the most tremor-affected hand are included, along with metadata spreadsheets and code to reproduce the associated paper.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh  jcavanagh@unm.edu

datasets.name: Siefert2024
datasets.description: Sleep EEG recordings from 34 participants who underwent Targeted Memory Reactivation (TMR) during sleep, collected to examine whether memory reactivation acts holistically on object memory. Event files describe the cueing sounds and the corresponding satellite objects, including blocked, interleaved, and uncued categories. The data are organized in BIDS format using the FieldTrip data2bids function.
datasets.authors: Elizabeth M. Siefert, Sindhuja Uppuluri, Jianing Mu, Marlie C. Tandoc, James W. Antony, Anna C. Schapiro

datasets.name: Resting-State EEG in Parkinson's Disease and Healthy Controls
datasets.description: This dataset contains eyes-open resting-state EEG recordings from individuals with Parkinson's disease and healthy controls. It comprises 358 recordings from 312 participants, with some participants recorded across multiple sessions to allow longitudinal analyses. Participant demographics and session-level clinical measures (MoCA, UPDRS Part III, disease duration, levodopa equivalent daily dose) are provided alongside BIDS-formatted BrainVision data.
datasets.authors: Brooke Yeager, Arturo Espinoza, Rachel Cole, Christina Weber, Ergun Uc, James Cavanagh, Nandakumar Narayanan

datasets.name: RSVP with flankers - sentences with semantic and syntactic violations
datasets.description: EEG dataset recorded during rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) of sentences with flanking words, in which the critical center word was shown between grey flanker words. Sentences contained subject-verb agreement violations, semantic violations, double violations, word-order violations, or no violation (controls). The dataset supports research on sentence processing and parafoveal word processing during reading.
datasets.authors: Emily M. Akers, Katherine J. Midgley, Phillip J. Holcomb, Karen Emmorey

datasets.name: MET - Music-Induced Emotion EEG Dataset
datasets.description: The MET dataset contains EEG recordings from 20 participants during a resting-state session and twenty music-listening sessions, each featuring a different song. Each music session lasts 130 seconds, with 5 seconds before onset, 120 seconds of playback and 5 seconds after offset. The data were recorded with a 128-channel system, then preprocessed and reduced to 66 channels, and are organized according to BIDS.
datasets.authors: Weng Lam, Cheang

datasets.name: FUS and Tactile Neuromodulation in NHP VPL - Electrophysiology
datasets.description: Intracranial electrophysiology recordings from the ventral posterolateral (VPL) thalamus of macaques, collected with a 32-channel linear probe during transcranial focused ultrasound (FUS) neuromodulation and tactile stimulation. FUS was targeted either to VPL thalamus or to insular cortex while recording remained in VPL. The dataset includes spiking and local field potential recordings supporting a study of FUS effects on primate thalamic activity.
datasets.authors: Ning Zheng, Pai-Feng Yang, M. Anthony Phipps, Jiro Kusunose, Arabinda Mishra, Jixin Xia, William Rodriguez, Allen T. Newton, Benoit M. Dawant, John C. Gore, Charles F. Caskey, Li Min Chen

datasets.name: EEG RKI
datasets.description: A collection of electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 15 students (8 male, 7 female, aged 21-23) performing essay-writing tasks. The task was designed to assess cognitive conditions such as creativity, memory, and critical thinking under different generative AI interaction conditions. The dataset supports studies of brain connectivity during student learning processes with Gen-AI.
datasets.authors: Achmad Imam Kistijantoro, Lianna G. H. Margareta, Haura R. Haminullah, Qurotul Uyun, Fani Eka Nurtjahjo, Iwan Kustiawan, Didin Wahyudin, Nur Ahmadi, Ayu Purwarianti

datasets.name: NeuralEcho MACS high-density communication-related EEG dataset
datasets.description: High-density (127-channel) EEG recordings from 30 healthy, right-handed, native Chinese-speaking adults performing imagined and executed vocalization and writing tasks. Stimuli were four Chinese strokes (heng, shu, pie, na) and four English letters (a, b, c, d). The factorial design crossed task mode, action, script and token identity, yielding 32 event-coded conditions and 15,360 task events. The release also includes EEGLAB preprocessing derivatives and subject-level machine-learning exports.
datasets.authors: Huang Jinfeng, Kangqiao Liu, Li Zhongjie, Jin Yongdong
datasets.eeg_reference: M1 and M2 bilateral mastoid electrodes
datasets.placement_scheme: Shared 127-channel template montage derived from 127cn.csv; coordinates were not digitized separately for each participant

datasets.name: Random and Sequential Order Finger Motor Imagery
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 20 participants performing a novel finger motor imagery paradigm in which cues for individual fingers were presented in random and sequential order blocks. The order of blocks was counterbalanced across participants. Data were acquired with a 65-channel g.tec system at 512 Hz and organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Damm, Laura Marie, Jiang, Dai, Demosthenous, Andreas

datasets.name: Appleseed Audiobook MEG
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 12 participants listening to continuous narrative speech, plus an empty-room recording, organized in BIDS format. The dataset was collected to test whether speech processing relies on local, context-independent predictive models, unified predictive models, or both in parallel. It includes stimulus annotations, gammatone features, and derivatives such as FreeSurfer outputs, predictor objects, and processing scripts.
datasets.authors: Brodbeck, Christian, Bhattasali, Shohini, Cruz Heredia, Aura AL, Resnik, Philip, Simon, Jonathan Z, Lau, Ellen

datasets.name: EEG Moments Dataset (EMD)
datasets.description: The EEG Moments Dataset (EMD) contains EEG responses from 6 human subjects viewing 1,102 three-second naturalistic videos presented with their audio tracks. Each subject viewed the 1,000-video training set 6 times and the 102-video test set 24 times. Eye tracking (gaze and pupil size) was recorded simultaneously. The videos are human-annotated with object, scene, action, text description, memorability labels, and the dataset is the EEG companion to the BOLD Moments fMRI dataset.
datasets.authors: Alessandro T. Gifford, Pablo Oyarzo, Anne W. Zonneveld, Christina Sartzetaki, Iris I.A. Groen, Radoslaw M. Cichy

datasets.name: emg2pose: Surface EMG and Hand Pose
datasets.description: This dataset is a NEMAR re-host and EMG-BIDS conversion of the public emg2pose release from Meta Reality Labs. It contains 2 kHz, 16-channel wrist surface electromyography recordings paired with hand pose labels (joint angles) captured by a 26-camera motion-capture system. The release spans 193 users, 370 hours, and 29 behavioral stages, supporting benchmarking of sEMG-based hand pose estimation.
datasets.authors: Sasha Salter, Richard Warren, Collin Schlager, Adrian Spurr, Shangchen Han, Rohin Bhasin, Yujun Cai, Peter Walkington, Anuoluwapo Bolarinwa, Robert Wang, Nathan Danielson, Josh Merel, Eftychios Pnevmatikakis, Jesse Marshall, Alexandre Gramfort

datasets.name: BEETL Competition 2021 Motor Imagery Dataset B — transfer learning benchmark
datasets.description: Beetl2021-B is a preprocessed 32-channel EEG dataset from the NeurIPS 2021 BEETL competition, built to benchmark transfer learning for motor imagery decoding. It contains recordings from 2 healthy subjects performing four-class motor imagery (left hand, right hand, feet, rest) at 200 Hz, totaling 1590 trials. The dataset supports evaluation of cross-subject and cross-dataset generalization and domain adaptation in brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Xiaoxi Wei, A. Aldo Faisal, Moritz Grosse-Wentrup, Alexandre Gramfort, Sylvain Chevallier, Vinay Jayaram, Camille Jeunet, Stylianos Bakas, Siegfried Ludwig, Konstantinos Barmpas, Mehdi Bahri, Yannis Panagakis, Nikolaos Laskaris, Dimitrios A. Adamos, Stefanos Zafeiriou, William C. Duong, Stephen M. Gordon, Vernon J. Lawhern, Maciej Śliwowski, Vincent Rouanne, Piotr Tempczyk

datasets.name: Carzaniga-2025-foundation-10.48550/arxiv.2506.20354
datasets.description: Long-term pre-surgical intracranial EEG recordings from 50 patients with pharmacoresistant epilepsy, recorded at the Sleep-Wake-Epilepsy-Center of Inselspital, University of Bern, in collaboration with ETH Zurich. The dataset comprises about 6672 hours of continuous iEEG with 460 expert-annotated electrographic seizures. Data are fully anonymized, with channels in original recording order and no electrode locations disclosed, and are converted to BIDS in BrainVision format.
datasets.authors: Francesco Carzaniga, Michael Hersche, Abu Sebastian, Kaspar Schindler, Abbas Rahimi

datasets.name: BCCWJ-MEG
datasets.description: BCCWJ-MEG contains magnetoencephalography recordings from 35 right-handed native Japanese speakers who read Japanese newspaper articles word by word using rapid serial visual presentation. It is part of the BCCWJ-Brain collection, which also includes fMRI and EEG datasets acquired from separate participant groups with the same stimuli, enabling cross-modality comparison of language processing. Raw data, T1-weighted anatomical images, and preprocessed derivatives are provided.
datasets.authors: Yushi Sugimoto, Masayuki Asahara, Hyeonjeong Jeong, Akitake Kanno, Masatoshi Koizumi, Yohei Oseki

datasets.name: BCCWJ-EEG
datasets.description: BCCWJ-EEG contains electroencephalography recordings from 41 native Japanese speakers reading newspaper articles from the Balanced Corpus of Contemporary Written Japanese, presented word by word using rapid serial visual presentation. It is part of the BCCWJ-Brain collection, which also includes fMRI and MEG datasets acquired with the same stimuli in separate participant groups, enabling cross-modality comparisons of language processing. Preprocessed derivatives (filtered, ICA-cleaned, re-referenced, and evoked data) are provided.
datasets.authors: Yushi Sugimoto, Masayuki Asahara, Hyeonjeong Jeong, Akitake Kanno, Masatoshi Koizumi, Yohei Oseki

datasets.name: Hierarchical Priors in Perceptual Uncertainty and Psychosis Proneness - A Random-Dot Kinematogram task with low- and high-level priors
datasets.description: EEG-BIDS dataset of cue-locked EEG recordings and event annotations from 43 neurotypical adults performing a random-dot kinematogram motion discrimination task. The task dissociates low-level priors (implicitly learned tone-motion contingencies) from high-level priors (a cover story about tinted glasses) against a neutral baseline. The data support analyses of hierarchical priors with signal detection theory, drift-diffusion modeling, and occipital oscillatory and aperiodic EEG activity, alongside psychosis-proneness and psychological flexibility questionnaires.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Buchholz, Guido Hesselmann

datasets.name: Diffuse predictions stabilize and reshape neural code during memory encoding
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a visual working memory experiment in which participants judged whether a probe grating was rotated clockwise or counterclockwise relative to a memorized orientation. Color cues either predicted a 90° segment of possible orientations or gave no information about orientation. The dataset supports investigation of how diffuse predictions stabilize and reshape neural codes during memory encoding.
datasets.authors: Nursena Ataseven, Sahcan Ozdemir, Wouter Kruijne, Daniel Schneider, Elkan G. Akyurek

datasets.name: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with online experience sampling
datasets.description: A multi-session dataset of simultaneous EEG-fMRI recorded from 24 healthy adults aged 18-35 while they performed a gradual-onset continuous performance task (GradCPT) and a resting-state condition with intermittent multidimensional experience sampling. The same protocol was repeated on two days. Carbon wire loop sensors in the EEG cap support artifact removal. The dataset also includes ECG, behavioral responses, and mental health surveys. It supports study of attentional fluctuations, mind-wandering, and the test-retest reliability of EEG-fMRI relationships.
datasets.authors: Aaron Kucyi, Lotus Shareef-Trudeau, David Braun, Huiling Peng, Tiara Bounyarith, Janet Z. Li

datasets.name: EEG: Three armed bandit gambling task
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 23 healthy college students performing a three-armed bandit gambling task with oscillating reward probabilities. Each stimulus slowly shifts between low and high reinforcement probability in different phases, making the task suited to studying reward processing, reward prediction error, and novel task-set generation. Corrugator EMG and skin conductance were also collected for most participants.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh  jcavanagh@unm.edu

datasets.name: Auditory-Visual Shift Study
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG and EOG recordings from younger and older adults performing an interleaved auditory-visual dual-oddball attention-shift task. It was designed to examine how aging affects selective attention and responding to auditory versus visual stimulus streams. Participants performed focus-auditory, focus-visual, and shift-focus conditions, and the data are annotated with HED 8.0.0 in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Marissa Westerfield (data, curation), Scott Makeig (data, curation), Dung Truong (curation), Kay Robbins (curation), Arno Delorme (curation)
datasets.eeg_reference: average of the left- and right-mastoid

datasets.name: Multi-channel EEG recordings during a sustained-attention driving task
datasets.description: This dataset provides BIDS-EEG formatted raw recordings from 27 healthy adults performing a sustained-attention driving task in a virtual-reality driving simulator on a motion platform. It comprises 62 sessions (~82 hours) of 32-channel EEG at 500 Hz plus a vehicle lateral-position channel. Events mark randomly induced lane-departure onsets and the participants' steering responses, allowing study of reaction time as an index of fatigue and drowsiness.
datasets.authors: Zehong Cao, Chun-Hsiang Chuang, Jung-Kai King, Chin-Teng Lin
datasets.eeg_reference: Mastoid reference electrodes A1 and A2 placed on opposite lateral mastoid bones (both recorded as data channels).
datasets.placement_scheme: Modified international 10-20 system: 30 scalp electrodes plus mastoid references A1, A2 (classic nomenclature; T3/T4/T5/T6 = T7/T8/P7/P8).

datasets.name: A COVID-19 survivors and close contacts EEG dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains 173 resting-state EEG recordings from 86 healthy close contacts and 87 COVID-19 survivors, collected at the Cuban Neuroscience Center. It was created to characterize EEG signatures of COVID-19 survival relative to close contacts and the Cuban EEG normative database. Recordings use the standard 10-20 montage.
datasets.authors: Ana Calzada-Reyes, Eduardo Aubert-Vázquez, Lidice Galán-García, Maria Luisa Bringas-Vega, Trinidad Virués-Alba, Lidia Charroó-Ruiz, Yanely Acosta-Imás, Mitchell Valdés-Sosa, Laura Perez-Mayo, Joel Gutiérrez-Gil, Antonio Caballero-Moreno, Miguel Angel Alvarez, Norge Santiesteban, Javier Vicente Sánchez-Lopez, Annette Valdés-Virués, Elba Elvira Varona-Galindo, Elizabeth Méndez-Parra, Joviana Castro-Valiente, Leyanis Ramos-Hernández, Mabel Whilby-Santiesteban, Thelma Luz Carrillo-Alfonso, Shahwar Yasir, Yu Kin, Peng Ren, Dezhong Yao, Luo Cheng, Roberto Rodriguez-Labrada, Pedro Valdés-Sosa

datasets.name: Optimizing parameters for multiband ABRs to continuous speech
datasets.description: EEG dataset of multiband auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) derived from continuous 'peaky' speech, collected to identify optimal stimulus parameters. Experiment 1 compares zero-phase and chirp-phase speech profiles in normal-hearing adults, and Experiment 2 compares narrators with different fundamental frequencies (natural versus shifted to 100 Hz). Data include raw BrainVision EEG recordings, event files, and HDF5 stimulus and regressor files for deconvolution.
datasets.authors: Melissa J. Polonenko, Benjamin R. Eisenreich

datasets.name: EEG and hedonic responses to sonic-seasoning soundscapes
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings and hedonic (liking) ratings collected from participants exposed to sonic-seasoning soundscapes. Each participant has a combined recording with eyes-open and eyes-closed baselines followed by roughly 17 s exposures to jungle and deconstruct soundscapes. Liking ratings and baseline-state survey items are included in participants.tsv, and the stimulus audio is provided. An EEGLAB-ready processed version is provided as a derivative.
datasets.authors: Attila Pohlmann, Felipe Reinoso-Carvalho, Brayan Rodríguez

datasets.name: Raw resting-state EEG dataset with alternating eyes-open and eyes-closed recordings in healthy adults
datasets.description: Raw resting-state EEG recordings from healthy adults with no current psychiatric or neurological diagnosis, collected at the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid. Each participant completed four consecutive 5-minute runs alternating between eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions, in one of two counterbalanced sequences. Data are shared without preprocessing, only converted to BIDS from BDF format.
datasets.authors: Lydia Arana, Enrique Stern, Almudena Capilla

datasets.name: EEG Practice Set
datasets.description: A small practice EEG dataset collected during an EEG workshop organized by the Student Network for Neuroscience. It is intended solely for training and practice purposes and is not suitable for any formal analysis.
datasets.authors: Kähler, Asuka

datasets.name: EEG-Speech Brain Decoding Dataset
datasets.description: An EEG dataset paired with audio recordings for decoding speech from brain activity. It includes overt speech production, auditory listening, and listening followed by covert speech imagery tasks. Data were acquired with three EEG systems (g.tec g.Pangolin, g.tec g.SCARABEO, and ANT Neuro eego sports), together with EOG, EMG, and audio monitor channels.
datasets.authors: Motoshige Sato, Ilya Horiguchi, Masakazu Inoue, Kenichi Tomeoka, Eri Hatakeyama, Yuya Kita, Atsushi Yamamoto, Ippei Fujisawa, Shuntaro Sasai
datasets.placement_scheme: Custom left-hemisphere-dominant subset from a high-density g.Pangolin grid

datasets.name: Dataset: EEG-Controlled Exoskeleton for Walking and Standing - A Longitudinal Study of Healthy Individuals
datasets.description: A longitudinal brain-machine interface dataset from seven healthy adults who controlled a Rex Bionics lower-limb exoskeleton through motor imagery (walk/stop). Each participant completed nine sessions, each with an open-loop calibration training phase followed by twelve closed-loop control trials and extended 6-minute walk and stop imagery tasks. The dataset includes 60-channel EEG, EOG, IMU motion data from the head and exoskeleton, and exoskeleton control and feedback signals.
datasets.authors: Shantanu Sarkar, Kevin Nathan, Jose L. Contreras-Vidal

datasets.name: Grupos Pre and Post bids
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings organized in BIDS format, comparing groups measured before and after an intervention. It is intended to support analyses of pre- and post-intervention neural activity changes.
datasets.authors: MENGSHA QI

datasets.name: Grupos Pre and Post bids
datasets.description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings organized in BIDS format, collected from participants at pre- and post-intervention time points. It is intended to support analyses of intervention-related changes in brain activity across two experimental groups.
datasets.authors: MENGSHA QI

datasets.name: CrossModal Study
datasets.description: This dataset contains MEG recordings, with eye-tracking data acquired alongside, from healthy adults performing a cross-modal cue-target discrimination task. Participants were cued to prepare for an auditory or visual target. During a 3-second waiting interval, a 36 Hz frequency-tagged visual stimulus and a 40 Hz amplitude-modulated tone were presented. Targets appeared alone in one block and alongside a distractor from the other modality in the other block. The data were collected to study alpha oscillations and inhibition of early sensory processing during target preparation.
datasets.authors: Marion Brickwedde, Rupali Limachya, Roksana Markiewicz, Emma Sutton, Christopher Postzich, Kimron Shapiro, Ole Jensen, Ali Mazaheri

datasets.name: MorseEEG-ATP
datasets.description: MorseEEG-ATP is a multitask EEG dataset for studying auditory temporal processing and temporal pattern discrimination using Morse code stimuli. It contains synchronized 62-channel EEG and behavioral data from 32 healthy adults performing dot-count and first-last match discrimination tasks at three presentation rates (15, 30, and 40 characters per minute). The release includes raw and minimally preprocessed EEG, event annotations, behavioral measures, and analysis scripts in an EEG-BIDS structure.
datasets.authors: HZY, Research Team

datasets.name: CrossModal Study
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a cross-modal cueing study in which participants were cued to prepare for an auditory, visual, or non-specific target. A 3-second task-irrelevant delay followed the cue, during which a fixation cross was frequency-tagged at 36 Hz and a 40 Hz amplitude-modulated tone was played. Participants discriminated one of three gabor-patch or tone targets, sometimes with a distractor from the uncued modality. The dataset supports investigation of alpha oscillations and target preparation in cross-modal attention.
datasets.authors: Marion Brickwedde, Rupali Limachya, Roksana Markiewicz, Emma Sutton, Christopher Postzich, Kimron Shapiro, Ole Jensen, Ali Mazaheri

datasets.name: Different Doors
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 40 participants performing a two-door choice task with monetary gain or loss feedback. Blocks were either learnable, with one door yielding wins 60% of the time versus 10% for the other, or unlearnable, with outcomes drawn from learnable blocks and shuffled so that win and loss totals were matched. Each block was followed by a short survey on perceived door quality, enjoyment, motivation, and performance.
datasets.authors: Abigail Oloriz, Cameron D. Hassall

datasets.name: Dataset of emotion recognition using validated video stimuli with large-scale behavioral survey and MEG recordings
datasets.description: This dataset supports brain signal-based emotion recognition. It combines magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 23 participants who viewed 40 validated emotional video clips with a large-scale online behavioral survey of 500 respondents rating the same clips. Labels include Self-Assessment Manikin valence and arousal, discrete PrEmo emotion categories, and temporal highlight scene selections. Head digitization files with anatomical landmarks and HPI coil coordinates are provided for co-registration.
datasets.authors: Moon-A Yoo, Dong-Uk Kim, Soo-In Choi, Min-Young Kim, Sung-Phil Kim

datasets.name: ROAMM
datasets.description: ROAMM (Reading Observed At Mindless Moments) is a multimodal dataset of simultaneous EEG and eye-tracking recordings from 44 participants during naturalistic reading, with span-level mind-wandering annotations collected through a retrospective self-report paradigm. It serves as a benchmark for mind-wandering detection and EEG-to-text decoding, and supports research on how attention lapses degrade language decoding from brain activity. Synchronized machine-learning-ready data, reading stimuli and page-level comprehension scores are included.
datasets.authors: Haorui Sun, Ardyn Vivienne Olszko, Niharika Singh, David C. Jangraw

datasets.name: LDAEP and resting-state EEG in healthy women
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 69 healthy women (aged 19-40) collected at the Department of Psychology, University of Oslo, to study the relationship between hormonal contraceptive use and central serotonergic activity indexed by the loudness dependence of auditory evoked potentials (LDAEP). Each participant completed eyes-closed and eyes-open resting-state recordings, and 54 also completed an LDAEP auditory paradigm. Phenotype data cover hormonal contraceptive use, menstrual cycle phase, depressive symptoms (BDI-II), impulsivity (UPPS-P), and lifestyle factors.
datasets.authors: Henrik Normannseth, Stein Andersson, Christoffer Hatlestad-Hall

datasets.name: Resting-State EEG and Trait Anxiety
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recordings from 51 undergraduate participants at the University of Alberta, collected to examine how resting-state alpha and theta power and oscillatory dynamics relate to trait anxiety. Each participant completed alternating eyes-open and eyes-closed blocks, and the dataset includes preprocessed EEG along with questionnaire scores for anxiety and personality (STAI, TIPI, BIS/FFFS).
datasets.authors: Tamari Shalamberidze, Kyle Nash, Jeremy B. Caplan

datasets.name: EPOC
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating neurophysiological correlates of Post-COVID-19 condition in adults recruited from the COVIDOM/NAPKON-POP cohort in Schleswig-Holstein. Participants (N = 98) with prior PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection completed a battery of computerized cognitive tasks, including a psychomotor vigilance task, and a resting-state recording. Questionnaires on fatigue, anxiety, depression and sleep quality are included, and participants are grouped by presence or absence of self-reported cognitive symptoms. EEG recordings are missing for 3 participants (missing or corrupted files, or incomplete sessions).
datasets.authors: ["Christian Neumann", "Johanna Geritz", "Julian Keil", "Walter Maetzler", "Julius Welzel"]

datasets.name: EEG-Speech Brain Decoding Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings paired with vocal audio recordings from participants performing an overt speech production task, in which they read aloud visually presented text. It was collected to support brain decoding of speech from EEG. The data are organized in BIDS by recording date session and run, and include code for preprocessing, model training, and evaluation, as well as derivative outputs from a standard preprocessing pipeline.
datasets.authors: Motoshige Sato, Masakazu Inoue, Kenichi Tomeoka, Ilya Horiguchi, Eri Hatakeyama, Yuya Kita, Atsushi Yamamoto, Ippei Fujisawa, Shuntaro Sasai

datasets.name: Delineating neural contributions to EEG-based speech decoding
datasets.description: This dataset contains 128-channel EEG recordings acquired while participants produced one of five color words (green, magenta, orange, violet, yellow) under overt, minimally overt, and covert speech conditions. Each trial comprises five repetitions of the same word. Auxiliary channels (EOG, orbicularis oris EMG, microphone, display, trigger) support delineating neural versus non-neural contributions to EEG-based speech decoding. Sessions include calibration data for decoder training and online real-time decoding.
datasets.authors: Motoshige Sato, Yasuo Kabe, Sensho Nobe, Akito Yoshida, Masakazu Inoue, Mayumi Shimizu, Kenichi Tomeoka, Shuntaro Sasai

datasets.name: EEG Pre/Post Intervention Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings collected to examine changes in neural activity before and after an intervention. Participants are divided into three groups and recorded in pre- and post-intervention sessions. The data are organized in BIDS format with EDF recordings, JSON sidecars, and event files, supporting signal analysis, functional connectivity studies, and pre/post comparisons.
datasets.authors: Mengsha Qi

datasets.name: Multimodal dataset from the CMx7-MM Experiment
datasets.description: A raw multimodal dataset from 30 healthy right-handed adults performing a hierarchy of cognitive, motor, and combined cognitive-motor tasks across three sessions. It includes EEG, fNIRS, ECG, EMG, Biodex torque/kinematics, push-button responses, and subjective ratings of sleepiness and cognitive load. The data are organized in BIDS and are unprocessed exports from the acquisition systems.
datasets.authors: Zaineb Ajra, Grégoire Vergotte, Stéphane Perrey, Lilian Evra, Simon Pla, Gérard Dray, Jacky Montmain, Binbin Xu

datasets.name: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during smartphone interaction
datasets.description: A multimodal dataset of simultaneous 64-channel EEG, head-mounted eye-tracking, photoplethysmography (PPG), and galvanic skin response (GSR) recordings from 23 healthy adults. Participants took part in a naturalistic smartphone use condition and a standardized video viewing condition. Hardware TTL pulses synchronize the EEG and eye-tracking streams for temporal alignment across modalities.
datasets.authors: Prakash Mishra, Tapan K. Gandhi, Saurabh R. Gandhi

datasets.name: PD-EEG: Resting-State & Walking EEG in Parkinson's Disease
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 116 people with Parkinson's disease and 28 healthy controls, acquired at the Neurology Institute of Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center. Each participant was recorded during eyes-open resting state while sitting and during treadmill walking, with about 4 minutes per condition. The dataset also includes clinical measures such as MDS-UPDRS, MoCA, LEDD and the Color Trails Test, plus item-level UPDRS and longitudinal follow-up data for subsets of participants.
datasets.authors: Zoya Katzir, Daniel Vered, Inbal Maidan (inbalm@tlvmc.gov.il)

datasets.name: 1hrPVTdataset_allSubjects
datasets.description: This dataset contains scalp EEG recordings from healthy adults during one hour of stimulation. Conditions were 40 Hz audiovisual flicker, no flicker (control), or randomized flicker (sham). Participants performed a psychomotor vigilance task throughout the session.
datasets.authors: Matthew Attokaren, Annabelle Singer

datasets.name: Joint agency EEG dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioural and dual-EEG hyperscanning recordings from pairs of participants performing a musical joint action task. Pairs performed musical duets and constant pitch sequences on electronic music boxes and rated their sense of joint agency on each trial. The data support investigation of the cognitive and neural signals underlying joint agency, and include synchronization performance measures and event markers.
datasets.authors: Zijun Zhou, Anna Zamm, Justin Christensen, Vinesh Rao, Janeen Loehr

datasets.name: A common neural mechanism underlies experiences of passage of time
datasets.description: Raw EEG and behavioral recordings in BIDS format, accompanying the study 'A common neural mechanism underlies experiences of passage of time' (Jording et al.). The dataset contains per-subject BrainVision EEG recordings (.vhdr/.vmrk/.eeg), behavioral data, scans listings, and source data, and is intended for investigating the neural mechanisms underlying the experience of the passage of time. Task, participant, and equipment details beyond this are not specified in the source metadata.
datasets.authors: [Unspecified]

datasets.name: Comprehensive methodology for sample enrichment in EEG biomarker studies for Alzheimer’s risk classification
datasets.description: EEG dataset accompanying the PLOS ONE article 'Comprehensive methodology for sample enrichment in EEG biomarker studies for Alzheimer's risk classification' (Henao Isaza, Aguillon, Tobón Quintero, Lopera, & Ochoa Gómez, 2026). The recordings support a methodology for enriching samples in biomarker studies that classify Alzheimer's disease risk from EEG features. Data are stored in BIDS format (BrainVision .vhdr/.eeg/.vmrk files with accompanying metadata) and released under a CC0 license.
datasets.authors: Verónica Henao Isaza, Carlos Andrés Tobón Quintero, John Fredy Ochoa Gómez

datasets.name: EEG dataset on consumer responses to extreme versus traditional marketing videos
datasets.description: EEG recordings from ten participants who viewed six marketing videos from three companies (Red Bull, GoPro, Columbia Sportswear). The videos were either traditional product-focused advertisements or 'extreme' authentic documentary-style content. The dataset supports research on neural correlates of consumer responses to different marketing video styles.
datasets.authors: Allison Edit, Attila Pohlmann
datasets.eeg_reference: CMS/DRL reference (Common Mode Sense/Driven Right Leg; active reference configuration).
datasets.placement_scheme: 10-20 (modified; 10-10 subset positions: AF3, F7, F3, FC5, T7, P7, O1, O2, P8, T8, FC6, F4, F8, AF4)

datasets.name: A subset of large-scale EEG dataset (India + Tanzania)
datasets.description: A subset of a large-scale field EEG collection from India and Tanzania, including participants ranging from Hadzabe hunter-gatherers to office workers. Recordings are accompanied by metadata such as age, Mental Health Quotient (MHQ) score, income and sex. The parent program used trained nonspecialist teams and daily automated data-quality feedback to collect EEG at high throughput and low cost, with quality comparable to lab benchmark datasets.
datasets.authors: John Mary Vianney, Shailender Swaminathan, Jennifer Jane Newson, Dhanya Parameshwaran, Narayan Puthanmadam Subramaniyam, Swaeta Singha Roy, Revocatus Machunda, Achiwa Sapuli, Santanu Pramanik, John Victor Arun Kumar, Pramod Tiwari, G. Nelson Mathews Mathuram, Laurent Boniface Bembeleza, Joyce Philemon Laiser, Winifrida Julius Luhwago, Theresia Pastory Maduka, John Olais Mollel, Neema Gadiely Mollel, Adella Aloys Mugizi, Isaac Lwaga Mwamakula, Raymond Edwin Rweyemamu, Upendo Firimini Samweli, James Isaac Simpito, Kelvin Ewald Shirima, Anand Anbalagan, Suresh Kumar Arumugam, Vinitha Dhanapal, Kanimozhi Gunasekaran, Neelu Kashyap, Dheeraj Kumar, Durgesh Pandey, Poonam Pandey, Arunkumar Panneerselvam, Sonam Rai, Porselvi Rajendran, Santhoshkumar Sekar, Oliazhagan Sivalingam, Prahalad Soni, Pushpkala Soni, Tara C. Thiagarajan

datasets.name: HAD-MEEG
datasets.description: HAD-MEEG is a magnetoencephalography (MEG) and electroencephalography (EEG) dataset on human action recognition. It extends the Human Action Dataset fMRI resource (HAD-fMRI) and was recorded in the same 30 participants with the same stimuli, 21,600 video clips spanning 180 categories of human action. The millisecond temporal resolution of M/EEG complements the spatial precision of fMRI, enabling spatiotemporal study of the neural mechanisms of action recognition.
datasets.authors: Guohao Zhang, Sai Ma, Ming Zhou, Shaohua Tang, Shuyi Zhen, Zheng Li, Zonglei Zhen

datasets.name: Sterotactic Focused Ultrasound Mesencephalotomy for the Treatment of Head and Neck Cancer Pain
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG and MRI recordings from patients with head and neck cancer pain who underwent stereotactic focused ultrasound mesencephalotomy. It is organized in BIDS format with HED annotations. The README is an unfilled template, so acquisition details are not documented.
datasets.authors: W. Jeffrey Elias, Chang-Chia Liu, Divine Nwafor, Patrick H. Finan, Mark Quigg, Shayan Moosa

datasets.name: EEGEyeNet Dataset
datasets.description: A BIDS-standardized subset of the EEGEyeNet dataset containing simultaneously recorded EEG and eye-tracking data from a single subject. The original EEGEyeNet resource was designed as a dataset and benchmark for eye movement prediction from EEG. This version was reformatted to BIDS to support reuse and standardized analysis.
datasets.authors: Martyna Beata Płomecka, Ard Kastrati, Nicolas Langer

datasets.name: Personalized smartphone notifications bias auditory salience across processing stages
datasets.description: This EEG dataset investigates how personalized smartphone notification sounds bias auditory salience across successive stages of sensory and cognitive processing. Participants completed an auditory oddball experiment, allowing comparison of neural responses to personally relevant notification sounds against other auditory stimuli.
datasets.authors: Prakash Mishra, Tapan K Gandhi, Saurabh R. Gandhi

datasets.name: tACS for Patients with Post-Stroke Anomia
datasets.description: EEG recordings from two chronic post-stroke anomia patients (one left-hemisphere and one right-hemisphere lesion) who took part in an 8-week individualized transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) intervention. Stimulation and non-stimulation phases alternated every two weeks in a single-case ABAB design. EEG was recorded during a picture naming task at intervention weeks and follow-ups to assess effects of tACS on naming accuracy and latency.
datasets.authors: Maria Martzoukou, Nefeli K. Dimitriou, Binbin Xu, Malo Renaud-d’Ambra, Anastasia Nousia, Alexandre Aksenov, Anne Beuter, Grigorios Nasios

datasets.name: Visual Occlusions with Treadmill Walking Speeds EEG
datasets.description: Mobile EEG dataset from 15 healthy young adults who stood still and walked on a treadmill at 0.4, 0.8, 1.2, and 1.6 m/s while viewing a static projected scene through liquid crystal lenses that alternated between transparent and opaque states. The study examines how electrocortical responses to intermittent visual occlusions, in particular alpha synchronization, change with gait speed. It includes 120-channel scalp EEG, noise electrodes, neck EMG, insole ground reaction forces, and lower-back IMU data.
datasets.authors: Jonel Morris, Kenneth Cruz, Raydeep Kainth, Daniel Ferris

datasets.name: Cross-Environment Multi-Paradigm Motor Imagery EEG Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from motor imagery (left- and right-hand) tasks collected in different recording environments. The main dataset covers 84 healthy participants in a shielded laboratory and a simulated hospital environment, and is intended to study how environmental variability affects EEG-based brain-computer interface performance. A small supplementary dataset from 3 participants recorded in a space station environment extends the collection to a non-terrestrial, microgravity setting. Multiple paradigms are included: Graz, SSMVEP-MI, and hybrid video conditions.
datasets.authors: Sun Xinwei, Wang Kun, Pan Lincong, Cao Yupei, Meng Lin

datasets.name: EEG-Asymmetries Dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 100 healthy adults collected to study hemispheric asymmetries, specifically the relationship between N1 lateralization and alpha asymmetry. Each participant completed an eight-minute resting-state session with alternating eyes-open and eyes-closed periods. They then completed four lateralized visual tasks (words, faces, emotions, houses) with left- and right-hand responses.
datasets.authors: Petunia Reinke, Lisa Deneke, Sebastian Ocklenburg

datasets.name: Multimodal Cognitive Workload n-back Task, 4 Difficulties
datasets.description: This dataset contains multimodal recordings from an n-back cognitive workload task with four difficulty levels (1-back to 4-back). It includes 19-channel mobile EEG, ECG, and Pupil Labs eye-tracking and pupillometry data, synchronized with Lab Streaming Layer. Twenty participants were recorded and 18 are released, with two excluded for data quality failures. The data were converted from XDF to BIDS.
datasets.authors: Matthew Barras, Liam Booth
